Rust: Memory Safety Without a Garbage Collector

Rust is a systems programming language focused on safety, speed, and
concurrency. Its ownership model enforces memory safety at compile time,
eliminating entire classes of bugs such as use-after-free and data races
without relying on a garbage collector.

Ownership, borrowing, and lifetimes are the three pillars of this model.
Together they let the compiler prove that references are always valid, so
programs can run with the performance of C and C++ while remaining memory
safe by construction.
